dedupe_keys.name: imda mobile service quality measurements 3g quality of service indicators and quarterly 4g coverage surveys singapore

description: The Infocomm Media Development Authority measures the service quality of Singapore's three mobile operators, M1, Singtel and StarHub, against its quality of service standards. For 3G, data.gov.sg holds monthly operator indicators from 2013 to 2016: nationwide outdoor service coverage (share of samples at or above -100 dBm), average drop call rate over a 100 second call (standard below 1 percent) and call set-up success rates across all cells from 2007 to 2016. For 4G, IMDA ran quarterly measurement surveys with mobile handsets over test routes covering all major and minor roads, expressways, parks and open spaces, road and MRT tunnels and randomly chosen buildings, and published one PDF per quarter from Q4 2014 to Q4 2018. The Q4 2018 sheet, for example, reports how many of 60 tested buildings achieved more than 85 percent in-building coverage at -109 dBm or better (55, 60 and 58 of 60 for the three operators). A 4G quality of service standard for nationwide outdoor coverage applies from 1 July 2016. Coverage: Singapore, by operator. Format and access: CSV on data.gov.sg under the Singapore Open Data Licence and one-page PDF result sheets on the IMDA site, free. Caveats: the published series end in 2016 (3G) and 2018 (4G); results are operator-level pass rates, not maps or individual measurements; later 5G monitoring was not found on the pages read. Simulation uses: indoor and tunnel coverage reliability benchmarks for mobile service models and for dense urban resilience studies. Related records: the Korea 5G service quality evaluation, the TRAI independent drive tests and the MCMC broadband experience surveys report comparable regulator measurements.
licence: Singapore Open Data Licence (data.gov.sg); IMDA website terms for the PDFs
